members.title: Is violence the path back to politics?
members.lead: The activities-banned Awami League wants to return to politics. It is not unusual for a political party to have such an aspiration. However, the party whose activities were banned due to their prolonged authoritarian rule, destruction of state institutions and the electoral system, practices of abduction and murder to suppress opposition politics and opinions, and the fresh memory of indiscriminate killings during the 24th uprising, should not find it surprising if certain conditions are attached to their return to politics. The foremost condition is to ensure the trial of these misdeeds and crimes against humanity and to penalise the guilty individuals. Subsequently, the people will want to see if the party responsible for these incidents is remorseful, and whether they will apologise or express regret. The return of the Awami League to politics is intertwined with these issues. The ousting of Awami League was not just the fall of a government; it was a collective rejection by the people against a repressive and authoritarian political system. In Bangladesh's politics, there is no precedent for apologising for mistakes or wrongdoings. Therefore, it is certain that the Awami League too will not tread this path. For crimes against humanity committed in 1971, Jamaat-e-Islami has never formally apologised. However, Jamaat had to wait a long time to return to politics and had to pay a heavy price for it. Most importantly, the party still has to carry the burden of that stigma. . It has not even been two and a half years since the 24th uprising, and already the Awami League, which was toppled by that uprising and sought refuge in India, is wanting to return to politics through the issue of Sheikh Hasina's return to the country. And for this, the strategy that the party has chosen is violence. members.title: Awami League miscreants tried to set my house on fire in Khagrachhari: Shadik Kayem
members.lead: Dhaka University Central Students’ Union (DUCSU) Vice-President Shadik Kayem has alleged that activists of the activities-banned Awami League attempted to set his house on fire in Khagrachhari with petrol bombs and kerosene late Saturday night. He made the allegation in a post on his verified Facebook page at around 5:30 am on Sunday. Shadik Kayem wrote, “At around 3:30 am tonight, terrorists from the banned fascist Awami League attempted to set my house on fire in Khagrachhari using petrol bombs and kerosene.” .Constitution to be amended if necessary to permanently ban Awami League. He said his parents were at home at the time of the incident. According to his post, the attackers threw petrol bombs around the house and poured kerosene in front of the door before attempting to set the entire house ablaze. The fire was extinguished by local residents before it could spread inside the house. His parents escaped serious harm, he said. Sadik Kayem, who is the Jamaat-e-Islami-nominated mayoral candidate for Dhaka South City Corporation, further alleged that, "Supporters of killer Hasina, who is alienated from the people, believe they would regain political relevance by attacking, threatening and intimidating July uprising supporters." .Why the government is not cracking down on Awami League sabotage yet, and its strategy. He wrote that they were seeking revenge against the people through petrol bombs, arson and cowardly attacks under the cover of darkness. He said such clandestine acts of violence would not deter them but strengthen their resolve. Declaring that fascist Awami League politics would not be allowed to return to Bangladesh, Shadik Kayem wrote that this was their ultimate position. He added that they would ensure the political demise of what he called the Awami League’s evil forces in Bangladesh in the near future. . members.title: PM to hold dialogue with political parties soon
members.lead: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has taken an initiative to hold dialogue with anti-fascist political parties that took part in the July mass uprising. The dialogue may begin soon, according to several sources at the Prime Minister’s Office and senior officials in the government. Sources said that, in the wake of sabotage by the Awami League whose activity is banned, separate discussions or dialogues with different political parties are being planned over the next few days to foster national unity. The talks are expected to take place at the state guesthouse Jamuna. Opposition Leader and Jamaat-e-Islami Ameer Shafiqur Rahman, and National Citizen Party (NCP) Convener and Chief Whip of the opposition in parliament Nahid Islam, are currently abroad. . Responsible sources said the ruling BNP and the Prime Minister’s Office have already started preparations to organise the dialogue. The Prime Minister’s political dialogue may begin tomorrow, Monday, with a discussion with the NCP. . They may return to the country in the next few days. The dialogue is expected to begin after their return. However, sources from the government and the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) said the political parties are to be invited and the specific agenda of the discussions have yet to be finalised. Sources among Jamaat-e-Islami and NCP leaders said NCP Convener Nahid Islam will return to Dhaka from London this evening, Sunday. He left for the United Kingdom on 13 November. Opposition Leader Shafiqur Rahman, meanwhile, travelled to Australia last Friday. He will go to Malaysia from there and is expected to return to the country on 26 November. .Leader of Opposition advises PM to hold dialogue with political parties. There have been clandestine crude bomb attacks, arson attacks on vehicles, several police facilities, a number of Grameen Bank branch offices, and the homes of BNP MPs and leaders.
